Description
At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. This is where ambition meets opportunity and, where the impact of what you build helps define what comes next, for customers and for you.
What's in it for you? An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.
About The Team
Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon at Amazon - including Graviton (our server processors), Trainium and Inferentia (our machine learning training and inference accelerators), and the Nitro system that powers modern EC2. We own the full stack, from silicon through the software that makes it work (compilers, runtimes, drivers, and the frameworks that let customers run workloads on our hardware). As a Software Development Engineer I, you'll write the software that turns custom silicon into products used by millions.
Where You Might Land
Annapurna has software teams spanning the full stack, and we work to place you on a technical team aligned with your interests and strengths. Example teams and focus areas include:
Compiler development for ML accelerators (Neuron SDK, MLIR, LLVM)
ML runtimes and frameworks (integration with PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow)
Low-level systems software, firmware, and device drivers
Performance optimization and kernel development for custom silicon
Distributed training and inference infrastructure
Once you join, we partner with you and our hiring managers to match you to a team where your background and interests fit best, so your project is something you're genuinely excited to work on.
As an SDE I, you'll contribute to real production software, which may include:
Designing, implementing, and testing software across the stack - from low-level systems code to compilers, runtimes, and tooling
Writing efficient, maintainable code in languages such as C, C++, or Python
Optimizing software performance on custom hardware (Graviton, Trainium, Inferentia)
Debugging complex issues across the hardware-software boundary
Collaborating with hardware, compiler, and systems teams to deliver features end-to-end
Documenting your work and presenting results to the team
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master's degree program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, with a final graduation date of May 2027 or later
Programming experience in at least one modern language such as C, C++, Java, or Python
Coursework or project experience in data structures, algorithms, and software design
Understanding of core computer science fundamentals: operating systems, computer architecture, or systems programming
Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master's degree with a focus on systems, compilers, computer architecture, or high-performance computing
Experience with low-level or systems programming in C/C++ (memory management, concurrency, performance optimization)
Familiarity with compilers (MLIR, LLVM, TVM), ML runtimes, operating systems internals, or distributed systems
Exposure to machine learning frameworks and an understanding of how models run on hardware
Prior internship, research, or open-source contribution experience in systems, compilers, or ML infrastructure

Responsibilities
The Agentic Platform team is the force-multiplier for TikTok USDS JV's Infrastructure and Platform teams. We are building and deploying a highly advanced, autonomous layer of AI agents that act as "virtual team members" for SRE, Systems, Capacity, Networking and operational roles. Our agents don't just alert—they observe signals, diagnose root causes, execute complex machine remediations, and safely report outcomes to humans and core cloud infrastructure.
Operating under the principle that "agents own the toil, humans own the judgment," we are a 0 to 1 engineering team tackling massive infrastructure challenges. Over the next 6 months, our mission is to eliminate over 50% of manual ticket-handling effort across USDS and measurably optimize critical machine infrastructure (GPU, HDFS) and Disaster Recovery (DR) readiness metrics.
We are looking for a Software Engineer who thrives in fast-paced environments and is passionate about building production-grade automation. In this role, you will help build the foundational services, integrations, and tools that power our autonomous agents, enabling the fleet to heal itself at scale.
Responsibilities
- Core Service Development: Design, build, and deploy production-grade, highly concurrent services that form the core of the Agentic Platform runtime, tool registry and integrations.
- Workflow Automation & Triage: Apply the Agentic Platform to specific workflows, scaling diagnostic playbooks and enable intelligent triage, isolation, and auto-healing of complex hardware and system faults (e.g., FS read-only, disk, RDMA, and network interface cards).
- Systems Integration: Integrate our AI agent framework with core internal logging, monitoring, and ticketing systems (e.g., SAOS, Fault, Tianshu, and Alto).
- System Reliability & Observability: Embed telemetry, monitoring, and metrics into every agent to track throughput, fault rates, and time-to-remediation, ensuring highly visible platform performance.
- CI/CD & Operational Excellence: Maintain robust automated testing and CI/CD pipelines to deploy agents safely into production under strict compliance and data-boundary guardrails.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualification(s):
- BS/MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline with industry experience.
- 2+ years of experience as a software engineer with proven contributions to team-based projects, ideally in an infrastructure, automation, or backend platform role.
- Solid programming skills, with deep proficiency in Python, Go, or C/C++ and a strong grasp of data structures and algorithms.
- Experience building and maintaining RESTful APIs, microservices, or backend automation workflows.
Preferred Qualification(s):
- Agentic Frameworks: Exposure to or strong interest in LLM orchestration, custom agent architectures, or API-driven automation.
- Infrastructure & SRE Familiarity: Basic understanding of Linux internals, telemetry pipelines (logging/metrics), and SRE concepts like MTTR and fault isolation.
- Distributed Systems: Knowledge of concurrent programming and distributed systems design.
About USDS
TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC is dedicated to the safety and security of millions of Americans who create, discover, and connect with what they love on the apps we operate. The Joint Venture has been established in compliance with the Executive Order signed by President Trump on September 25, 2025. Our foundation is a comprehensive data privacy and cybersecurity program we operate under defined safeguards to protect national security and secure U.S. user data, apps and the algorithm. We safeguard the U.S. content ecosystem, holding decision-making authority for trust and safety policies and moderation. USDS Joint Venture helps ensure Americans can continue to express their creativity, discover new hobbies and interests, and build thriving communities and businesses on a global scale.​
​

As such, the company is shifting from a hybrid work model to a fully in-person schedule up to 5 days a week.​
Why Join Us
Inspiring creativity is at the core of TikTok's mission. Our innovative product is built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Together, we create value for our communities, inspire creativity and bring joy - a mission we work towards every day.​
We strive to do great things with great people. We lead with curiosity, humility, and a desire to make impact in a rapidly growing tech company. Every challenge is an opportunity to learn and innovate as one team. We're resilient and embrace challenges as they come. By constantly iterating and fostering an "Always Day 1" mindset, we achieve meaningful breakthroughs for ourselves, our company, and our users. When we create and grow together, the possibilities are limitless. Join us.​

description_preview:
Description
At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. This is where ambition meets opportunity and, where the impact of what you build helps define what comes next, for customers and for you.
What's in it for you? An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.
About The Team
Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon at Amazon - including Graviton (our server processors), Trainium and Inferentia (our machine learning training and inference accelerators), and the Nitro system that powers modern EC2. We own the full stack, from silicon through the software that makes it work (compilers, runtimes, drivers, and the frameworks that let customers run workloads on our hardware). As a Software Development Engineer I, you'll write the software that turns custom silicon into products used by millions.
Where You Might Land
Annapurna has software teams spanning the full stack, and we work to place you on a technical team aligned with your interests and strengths. Example teams and focus areas include:
Compiler development for ML accelerators (Neuron SDK, MLIR, LLVM)
ML runtimes and frameworks (integration with PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow)
Low-level systems software, firmware, and device drivers
Performance optimization and kernel development for custom silicon
Distributed training and inference infrastructure
Once you join, we partner with you and our hiring managers to match you to a team where your background and interests fit best, so your project is something you're genuinely excited to work on.
As an SDE I, you'll contribute to real production software, which may include:
Designing, implementing, and testing software across the stack - from low-level systems code to compilers, runtimes, and tooling
Writing efficient, maintainable code in languages such as C, C++, or Python
Optimizing software performance on custom hardware (Graviton, Trainium, Inferentia)
Debugging complex issues across the hardware-software boundary
Collaborating with hardware, compiler, and systems teams to deliver features end-to-end
Documenting your work and presenting results to the team
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master's degree program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, with a final graduation date of May 2027 or later
Programming experience in at least one modern language such as C, C++, Java, or Python
Coursework or project experience in data structures, algorithms, and software design
Understanding of core computer science fundamentals: operating systems, computer architecture, or systems programming
Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master's degree with a focus on systems, compilers, computer architecture, or high-performance computing
Experience with low-level or systems programming in C/C++ (memory management, concurrency, performance optimization)
Familiarity with compilers (MLIR, LLVM, TVM), ML runtimes, operating systems internals, or distributed systems
Exposure to machine learning frameworks and an understanding of how models run on hardware
Prior internship, research, or open-source contribution experience in systems, compilers, or ML infrastructure

Data Engineer

Posted: September 24, 2026
About Pavago
Pavago connects businesses with skilled professionals to support their operational and technical needs. For this opportunity, Pavago’s client is seeking a Data Engineer to build and maintain scalable data infrastructure that powers analytics, reporting, and business decision-making.
About the Role
Pavago’s client is seeking a Data Engineer to design, build, maintain, and optimize reliable data pipelines and scalable data infrastructure.
The role focuses on ensuring seamless data flow from source systems into data warehouses, dashboards, and downstream applications while maintaining high standards of data quality, governance, performance, and scalability.
The ideal candidate combines strong software engineering fundamentals with analytical thinking and is comfortable collaborating across engineering, analytics, and business teams to deliver trustworthy, actionable data.
Key Responsibilities
Pipeline Development & Data Integration
Build, maintain, and optimize ETL/ELT pipelines using Python, SQL, or Scala.
Orchestrate workflows using Airflow, Prefect, Dagster, or similar tools.
Ingest structured and unstructured data from APIs, SaaS platforms, databases, files, and streaming systems.
Develop scalable connectors and automated data ingestion workflows.
Data Warehousing & Modeling
Manage and optimize cloud data warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift.
Design scalable data schemas using star and snowflake modeling techniques.
Implement partitioning, clustering, indexing, and other performance optimization strategies.
Build clean, analytics-ready datasets for business intelligence and reporting.

About The Role
This Research Engineer role sits at the intersection of privacy engineering and AI data infrastructure. You will own the full pipeline for detecting and removing sensitive information from raw, real-world data before it flows into processing, training, evaluation, and synthetic data workflows. The work is foundational: protecting privacy without destroying the structure and signal that make data valuable for training frontier AI agents.
What You'll Do
Build systems to detect PII, quasi-identifiers, credentials, and other sensitive information, and design appropriate transformations based on data type and downstream use case.
Develop and benchmark detection approaches that combine rules, statistical models, classifiers, and LLM-based methods.
Build production pipelines that anonymize raw data before it enters downstream processing, training, evaluation, or synthetic data generation workflows.
Create evaluation frameworks that measure privacy risk and retained data utility, including recall-weighted metrics, leakage tests, and adversarial re-identification attempts.
Design systems that remain robust to new data sources, schema drift, unusual formats, and sensitive information embedded in unexpected fields.
Collaborate with engineering, research, operations, and customers to translate privacy requirements into practical technical policies and safeguards.
What We're Looking For
2+ years of experience building reliable production data or ML systems in Python.
Hands-on experience with information extraction, named-entity recognition, classification, or related methods for detecting sensitive or rare content.
Experience building end-to-end data processing pipelines without a fully prescribed roadmap.
Strong experimental instincts with the ability to compare approaches across recall, precision, latency, cost, and downstream data utility.
Solid understanding of redaction, masking, pseudonymization, anonymization, and synthetic data generation, and when each is appropriate.
Experience designing systems that are robust to schema drift, unusual formats, and edge cases.
Familiarity with privacy-enhancing technologies such as differential privacy, k-anonymity, secure aggregation, or format-preserving encryption is a strong plus.
Experience with low-latency or high-throughput ML inference and data processing systems is a plus.

Reimagine the infrastructure of cancer care within a community that values integrity, inspires growth, and is uniquely positioned to create a more modern, connected oncology ecosystem.
We’re looking for a data and technology-oriented Software Engineer to help us accomplish our mission to improve and extend lives by learning from the experience of every person with cancer. Are you ready to be the next changemaker in cancer care?
What You'll Do
This role will design and develop technology within Flatiron’s engineering organization. This role will collaborate cross functionally with experts across a variety of functions to understand how to develop technology solutions that drive clinical outcomes either in the practice or research settings to understand their challenges and how technology can help solve them.
Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and stakeholders to deeply understand problems before jumping to solutions whilst balancing customer needs, technical constraints, and business priorities
Break down ambiguous requirements into well-scoped, actionable work, and ask clarifying questions and surface risks early
Design, implement, test, and deploy features end-to-end. Write clean, well-tested code that balances pragmatism with long-term maintainability
Investigate and resolve bugs by tracing issues to root causes, designing thoughtful fixes, and validating changes with automated tests
Participate in design and code reviews, giving and receiving constructive feedback that elevates team quality
Effectively leverage AI-assisted coding tools and modern technologies to accelerate development while applying critical judgment to validate outputs and maintain security, reliability, and code quality
Who You Are
You're a kind, passionate and collaborative problem-solver who values the opportunity to think beyond the way things are. You're excited by the prospect of working on difficult and meaningful problems each day. You seek and give candid feedback, and value the chance to make an important impact on cancer patients and society.
You’re a software engineer with 1-4 years of relevant professional experience
You hold a Bachelors, Masters, and/or Ph.D. in computer science or a related field
You are comfortable with ambiguity and always willing to teach and learn
You are excited to work in a fast moving environment, think creatively and be scrappy to get the job done
You have a nose for value and empathy for your customers
You have experience with languages like Python, C++, Java, and/or C#, but are also willing to pick up new programming languages as needed
You have some experience working with cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, or GCP
You have a good understanding of relational databases like PostgreSQL, MySQL, or MSSQL
You understand the purpose of “boring” technology (as described in this blog post) and are willing to use the right tools to get the job done
Extra credit
You have experience working in healthcare or exposure to healthcare-related standards like HL7
You have experience developing software with AI agents like Claude Code or Cursor
You have experience with containerized environments such as Docker, including image creation, orchestration, and production deployment.
You have experience building and maintaining data pipelines and modeling production datasets in Snowflake.
Where You’ll Work
In this hybrid role, you’ll have a defined work location that includes work from home and 3 office days set by you and your team. For more information on our approach to hybrid work, please visit the how we work website.
Life at Flatiron
At Flatiron Health, we offer a full range of benefits to support you and your loved ones so you can focus your working hours on improving cancer care and accelerating cancer research, and your non-working hours on everything else life has to offer:
Work/life autonomy via flexible work hours and flexible paid time off
Comprehensive compensation package
401(k) contribution to help you reach your retirement planning goals
Financial health resources including 1:1 financial advice
Mental well-being tools and services
Parental benefits and policies including family-building care and generous leave
Path to parenthood programs supporting fertility, adoption and surrogacy

About Rare Candy
Rare Candy is revolutionizing the $25 billion trading-card industry as the “friendly local game shop” in the palm of your hands. Collectors use our AI-powered card scanner, open their favorite chase cards with Instapacks, and keep track of them with our data-rich collection tools which showcases Pokémon, MTG, Lorcana, One Piece, and more. We've hit 10x revenue growth over the last 6 months, the business is profitable, and we're building the team to take this from a great product to a category-defining one.
We're a 10-person product team moving fast and looking for the next set of TCG-obsessed rock stars to join our team.
The Role
We're hiring a Fullstack Developer to help build the operations toolchain we use every day to manage our warehouse, inventory, and managing our Instapacks business.
You'll work closely with the CTO and engineering team to ship new tools and features for our operations team. This is a hands-on product engineering role for someone who loves solving logistic problems, has a background in GO and React, and wants to grow quickly inside a fast-moving startup.
You won't be handed endless tickets in a giant backlog. You'll work on real problems, learn from phenomenal backend engineers, and see your work go directly into the hands of passionate collectors.
If you love trading cards or collector communities, this is a role for you.
What Success Looks Like
First 30 days:
You get the various ops tools running locally, understand the core problems, and ship your first meaningful fixes or small features.
By day 90:
You're regularly shipping features for our Ops team with support from the CTO and principal engineer. You can take a well-scoped feature or improvement, ask the right questions, implement it cleanly, test it, and get it into the team's hands.
By the end of year one:
You've become the main point of contact for the most important part of our Instapack business. You've shipped meaningful improvements to our Ops toolchain, grown your Go and React craft, and earned ownership over increasingly business critical items.
What You'll Do
Build and improve our Ops toolchain to help support our entire Warehouse and Logistics team.
Fix bugs, improve bottlenecks, and raise the quality bar for Ops toolchain.
Work closely with ops and engineering to increase efficiency to hard problems.
Learn quickly, ask good questions, and communicate clearly when something is blocked, unclear, or ready for review.
A Day in Your Life at Rare Candy
You start the morning checking in with the warehouse team and reviewing feedback on a feature you shipped yesterday.
Mid-morning, you're pairing with other engineers on making improvements on various backend services.
After lunch, you're tightening up a dashboard, fixing an edge case, and testing the flow against real time operations.
Later in the day, you're in an operations discussion about how we want to launch a new game for Instapacks and how our toolchain needs to support it.
You close the day by opening a PR with a clear summary, and a note about what still needs review.
You Might Be a Fit If
You have around 3-5 years of fullstack development experience with Go.
You're comfortable building with React or other React frameworks.
You've worked with GraphQL, or you have enough API experience to ramp quickly.
You care about product quality and the little details that make tools easy to use and feel good.
You have experience building internal tools and understand the importance of understanding the customer to build the right thing.
You're comfortable in a fast-moving startup where priorities can shift and the best answer is often “figure it out, then make it better.”
You know the trading-card or collector world. You collect, play, rip packs, follow the market, or have real fluency in a similar collectible space.
What You'll Need to Thrive Here
You’re expected to take ownership of your role at Rare Candy and drive your own growth. That doesn’t mean doing it alone. You’ll have support, context, and mentorship along the way.
The systems are still evolving, the team is small, and your work will matter immediately. You'll need to be curious, detail-oriented, and comfortable learning by doing.
If you like to build internal tools, solve operational issues, and the idea of building tools you would actually want to use yourself, you'll do great here.
Why Join Us Now
Work on features collectors actually care about and are using everyday.
Get real ownership early in your career while learning directly from experienced engineering leadership.
Join a high-trust, low-ego team that ships fast, celebrates wins, and cares deeply about the hobby.
Competitive startup comp, meaningful equity upside, and a salary range of $140,000-$160,000.
Full benefits: health, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), and a wellness stipend.
A monthly dogfooding budget to spend on cards, because we hire people who love this hobby.
How to Apply
Apply through our Ashby posting and answer these:
Describe an internal tool you built. What did you own, what technical choices did you make, and what was the result?
Explain a bug you debugged. What made it tricky, how did you track it down, and what did you learn?
What trading-card or collector communities do you understand best? Tell us your favorite card, set, format, deck, rip, or collector niche.
Rare Candy is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate individuality, from Pikachu collectors to Planeswalker pros, and are committed to building an inclusive team.

E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life.
What you will do:
Implement and evaluate defined DSP and 5G NR physical-layer (PHY) functions for satellite communications over non-terrestrial networks (NTN), working from agreed specifications and technical guidance.
Develop and run PHY/link-level simulations to measure error rates, throughput, and acquisition and tracking performance under representative satellite channel conditions, including propagation delay, Doppler, noise, and RF impairments.
Develop, test, and optimize C/C++ DSP firmware for 5G NR PHY processing, meeting defined execution-time, memory, power, and numerical-accuracy requirements.
Create floating-point and fixed-point reference models, reproducible test vectors, and expected results for ASIC designers and verification engineers. Document interfaces, scaling, rounding, saturation, and other assumptions needed to compare implementations.
Contribute to SystemC transaction-level modeling (TLM) and high-level synthesis (HLS) development, including synthesizable implementations, with guidance from engineers experienced in these flows.
Support pre-silicon verification and new-chip bring-up by running regressions, comparing model, firmware, and hardware results, investigating discrepancies, and documenting fixes with ASIC, verification, and software engineers.
What you bring to this role:
Demonstrated DSP and digital-communications fundamentals, including sampling, filtering, modulation, OFDM, synchronization, channel estimation, and error-correction concepts. Evidence may come from academic, research, personal, or professional projects.
Ability to implement and debug numerical algorithms in C/C++, and to use Python or MATLAB for simulation, analysis, and test automation.
Working knowledge of wireless PHY processing and the ability to translate technical specifications into implementation and test cases; familiarity with the basic structure of a 5G NR PHY.
Understanding of fixed-point arithmetic, quantization, overflow, and numerical precision, with the ability to compare an implementation against a reference model.
Understanding of embedded software constraints, including execution time, memory use, and hardware/software interfaces, supported by practical implementation or debugging work.
Ability to build reproducible tests, use version control, document technical assumptions and results, and explain discrepancies during code and design reviews.
Bonus points for the following:
Experience with SystemC TLM, or with HLS tools to develop and verify synthesizable C/C++ or SystemC implementations.
Experience with 5G NR or NTN algorithms and specifications, satellite channel modeling, or compensation for Doppler and timing effects.
Experience with FPGA/ASIC verification, emulation, SDR platforms, chip bring-up, or laboratory validation of communication systems.
Experience with 5G NR MAC, PHY/MAC interfaces, scheduling interactions, or HARQ procedures.
Experience implementing and optimizing algorithms on vector DSPs, including SIMD intrinsics, vectorization, and efficient memory access.
Experience with low-power ASIC or firmware design, including reducing computation and data movement, managing idle states, or measuring power consumption.

You will support the operations and availability of your team’s artifacts by creating and monitoring metrics, escalating when needed, and supporting “keep the lights on” & on-call efforts.
You will contribute to a sense of community on your team by engaging in growth and development activities such as participation in the interview process.

You have a total of 1.5+ years of experience as a software engineer.
You have experience designing, developing and launching backend systems and are proficient in one of Python or Kotlin.
You are familiar with the building blocks of distributed systems, and the technologies like AWS, MySQL and Kubernetes.
You have mastered taking a simple problem or business scenario into a solution that interacts with multiple software components, and executing on it by writing clear, easily understood, well tested and extensible code.
You are comfortable navigating a large code base, debugging others' code, and providing feedback to other engineers through code reviews.
Your experience demonstrates that you take ownership of your growth, proactively seeking feedback from your team, your manager, and your stakeholders.
You have strong verbal and written communication skills that support effective collaboration with our global engineering team.
This position requires either equivalent practical experience or a Bachelor’s degree in a related field

About Us:-
Prometheum is building the market infrastructure that brings securities onto the blockchain. Our SEC-registered broker-dealer network carries a digital asset through its entire life, from issuance and distribution to qualified custody, correspondent clearing, and secondary market trading, all within U.S. securities law.
That work has put us first more than once. We became the first SEC-registered special purpose broker-dealer, and the first to trade ETH inside a traditional brokerage account. Those milestones rest on systems our engineers build every day, and we are searching for engineers like you to help us grow our team.
Role:-
Blockchain Engineer 2 - Full time W2
Salary Range:-
$130,000 - $165,000
Overview:-
As a Blockchain Engineer 2, you take ownership of a whole feature once an epic is agreed on. Epics come from the Architect and CTO, but they are shaped in team brainstorms where you are expected to bring a view, including what is happening across the blockchain and cryptography landscape and how it should change our approach. Once we have consensus, you break the work into pieces the team can pick up, get it ready to build, guide it through to release, and keep stakeholders honestly informed along the way. You will work with the Architect on technical design, with guidance from senior engineers as you grow into that part of the job.
We are a specialist team. Other teams depend on us for custody contracts, transaction signing and orchestration, and the key management that ties them together, work they cannot do themselves, so our output is measured by how well it serves those teams and the customers behind them, not by how much of it you shipped. When something is not moving, we expect you to say so early and come with options.
Our engineering team is fully remote.
Responsibilities:-
Build and maintain secure and optimized blockchain applications
Own epics end to end, from story writing and pointing through delivery and release
Build across many different languages taking on the large, complex problems in your team's scope
Report progress on your epic regularly and accurately, and raise risks before they become surprises
Partner with senior engineers on technical design, architecture decisions, and future epics
Demonstrate a passion for learning, building, and constantly improving cutting-edge applications
Communicate often to encourage tight and quick feedback loops and remove potential blockers
Use AI coding tools as a default part of your workflow, and review what they produce with the same rigor you would apply to your own code
Review teammates' code in a way that catches design concerns, edge cases, and test gaps
Work directly with neighboring systems throughout delivery, not just at the handoff
Investigate and resolve issues found in QA, UAT, and production
Qualifications:-
3 or more years of professional software engineering experience building and shipping production software
Strong blockchain fundamental knowledge including in-depth knowledge of top chains (i.e. Bitcoin and Ethereum)
Familiarity with basic cryptography commonly utilized by blockchains
Strong administrative/organizational skills (ability to effectively prioritize, manage time, and meet deadlines on multiple projects)
Automated testing as a habit rather than an afterthought
Hands-on experience with AI coding assistants, plus the judgment to know when their output is wrong
Clear written communication with a strong command of the English language, which matters more on a fully remote team
Able to reason through technical disagreements with evidence, and to update your view when the evidence shifts
Authorized to work in the U.S. or Canada
Able to pass a comprehensive background check, which is required for this role
Nice to have:-
Experience mentoring or onboarding other engineers
Background in finance, brokerage, trading, or custody
Exposure to regulated environments and the audit trails they require
Experience with Jira, Confluence, or similar
How we work:-
Fully remote engineering. We work together in real time, with overlapping hours for pairing, reviews, and ceremonies.
AI-forward. We actively champion AI and tooling that ships customer value faster without giving up quality. Engineers at every level are expected to use these tools well and to bring what they find back to the team.
Feedback is specific and regular. Quarterly reviews, weekly 1:1s, and a candid conversation when something is not landing, not a surprise at year end.

Stock options
Competitive vacation time, paid sick days, and time off for observed federal holidays
